messages:
acme_ops: Hey team — since last night's rollout our onboarding chat changed. Steps that used to be a 3-bullet checklist are now one paragraph and sometimes omit the security step. Happening for redwood-chat-2. Example request_id: req_2026-03-16-ACME-42. Anyone seen this?

maya: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the raw request body and the raw response you got? Also the SDK version and approximate token counts if available.

acme_ops: Pasting minimal repro (redacted) below. We compared to responses from Friday and it's notably different.

```json
{"model":"redwood-chat-2","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Onboard steps for new users: please return a numbered list with security step included."}],"temperature":0.0}
```

Raw response we get now (truncated):

"Welcome! To get started, create an account then set up your profile. Be sure to review security settings before proceeding"

Expected (Friday):

"1) Create account
2) Verify email
3) Configure security settings (enable 2FA)"

Token counts: input_tokens: 61, output_tokens: 78. SDK: js v0.14.2.

jordan: FYI we rolled a tokenizer normalization change in the hosted runtime on 2026-03-16 03:12 UTC (deploy ab12f3). It normalizes NBSP and zero-width spaces inside chat templates to avoid weird invisible chars. That can shift subtoken boundaries and in edge cases alter list markers recognition. tagging @eng-runtime.

eli: Can you confirm the exact template id / template text you pinned? The change doesn't alter model weights but tokenization offsets can change whether the model sees a leading bullet `1)` vs `1\u00A0)` etc. If your template included nonstandard spaces that got normalized, model conditioning could change.

acme_ops: Template we pinned: `onboard_v2` — below snippet (copied from UI):

```text
Welcome to Acme!
Please follow the steps:
1) Create an account
2) Verify email
3) Configure security settings
```

No intentional NBSPs. Wondering why behavior flipped only after rollout. Workaround: any header to force old tokenization?

maya: For a short-term workaround, set header `X-Template-Version: pre-normalize` or pin `template_version: 20260315` in the request. That will route to the prior template rendering path while we investigate. Please confirm if that restores the expected output.

acme_ops: Confirmed the workaround restores numbered list output. Thanks. We'll keep using that while you dig in.

support-bot: deploy-bot: rolled out redwood-runtime v1.3.2 to hosted (canary -> global) at 2026-03-16T03:12:14Z, release notes: tokenizer normalization, minor logging fixes.

ops-lead: We should treat as a customer-facing regression. If more customers are affected we should rollback the change or ship a patch. Creating jira INFR-9123 and tagging product + eng-runtime.

jordan: Repro steps for eng: run tokenizer locally against sample list inputs and compare pre/post. Example: `./tools/tokenize --model redwood-chat-2 --text "1)\u00A0Create account\n2) Verify email"` shows different token segmentation between branches. Example output diff: 

```
# before (tokens)
["1",")"," ","Create"," account"] -> 7 tokens
# after (tokens)
["1)","Create"," account"] -> 5 tokens
```

This subtle merge changes the model prefix the same way as trimming a space — for some prompts it changes whether the model emits a newline-delimited list vs inline sentence.

eli: I'll run head-to-head evals on our nightly suite with `onboard_v2` and a set of 120 prompts to measure drop in list-formation rate.

maya: Action plan: 1) eng-runtime triage regression, 2) enable template_version fallback for affected customers, 3) run canary sweep for other templates, 4) hotfix if >5% customers impacted or major regressions. ETA for hotfix 4 hours.

acme_ops: Appreciate the quick response and the workaround. Please keep us updated in this thread and on the ticket INFR-9123.

maya: Will do — tagging @acme_ops in the jira and will follow up after initial repros. :thumbsup:
